newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent eases as fundamentals suppress bounce.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent eases as fundamentals suppress bounce.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures edged lower in nervous, light trade on Thursday as an increasingly bearish fundamental picture dashed hopes of a bounce higher, brokers said.
April Brent traded 20 cents lower at $19.20 a barrel at 1307 GMT, while March gas oil was $1 off at $161.00 a tonne.

"There's really nothing out there in terms of the fundamentals to help the market higher," one broker said. "It's struggling." Brokers said a combination of poor physical demand, news of increased OPEC production and crude run cuts by a handful of European refineries had deepened the bearish tone.

"There is a general feeling that most nearby requirements are covered on both sides of the Atlantic, with upcoming maintenance programmes reducing demand," Lawrence Eagles at commodity brokers GNI said in their daily energy report.
"This tends to make the market look as if it could break lower in the meantime, even though it is extremely oversold," he added.

Crude oil production by OPEC rose 130,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 26.77 million in February from 26.64 million bpd in January, according to a Reuters survey of OPEC officials, oil companies and analysts released on Thursday.
The official OPEC output ceiling is fixed at 25.033 million bpd for the 11-member cartel.
News of crude throughput cuts at a handful of northwest European refineries due to poor margins also weighed on the market, traders said.
Shell has reduced crude runs at it Rotterdam refinery by 12-15 percent from recent levels of 350,000 bpd -- equivalent to nearly 50,000 bpd, trading sources said on Thursday.
Texaco Netherlands said it had deepened crude run cuts at the Nerefco refinery in Rotterdam it shares with British Petroleum to 12.5 percent.
The company controls 35 percent of the 400,000 bpd refinery so the cut is equivalent to 17,500 bpd.
